authoritative_for: Todo owns the durable identities, immutable provenance, routing and design decisions, current projections, lifecycle, database, installation, and digest behavior published by this provider.

Each Todo entry states the supported boundary for one public use, operation, or development outcome; Todo SQLite and the installed release remain the runtime authorities for actual records and behavior.
not_authoritative_for: Nucleus owns model execution, authentication, job state, and raw protocol history; Resend and the recipient provider own external email submission and receipt.
Source artifacts and independently stewarded systems remain authoritative for their own contents and current state, and Todo lifecycle markers do not prove implementation execution.

covers: All supported public Todo CLI outcomes for concern capture and routing research, umbrella reads and decisions, situation assessment, desired-state design, digest preview and send, installation and migration, and development in this release.
excludes: Help and version display, internal liaison and mailbox protocol details, implementation helpers, direct database access, external implementation execution, and upstream service behavior are outside this inventory claim.

shared_access_and_trust: Todo is a local current-user CLI over its selected SQLite database; model-assisted stages use only frozen bounded inputs through the separately installed Nucleus service.
Mutation, decision, deployment, migration, and external email effects require the exact authority and preconditions stated by the selected entry; catalog presence grants none of them.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Todo state can contain private directions, paths, evidence references, assessments, designs, notes, email metadata, and decision provenance and remains within the selected local database and installation boundary.
Nucleus may retain source and prompt content read during research, while Resend and the recipient provider retain the explicitly sent digest under their own policies.
compatibility_and_retirement: Provider release identifies the Todo release, entry contract version identifies public semantic compatibility, and SQLite schema version is a separate persistent-state contract.
Incompatible contract or persistent-state changes require versioning, migration or dependency updates, retained historical meaning, and documented rollback before older behavior is retired.
operational_limits: Todo has no daemon, workflow engine, implementation executor, or general project graph; model work is bounded research and external email is an explicit synchronous action.
No global latency, capacity, delivery-time, implementation-completion, or external-state freshness service-level objective is promised across this provider.
